question: Why is spotting delivery complications early at a primary health centre so crucial?

options.A: It ensures the family will pay the delivery fees on time

question: As a student nurse, why should you avoid shaking dirty bed linen in the air?

options.A: Shaking disperses dust and microorganisms into the surrounding room

options.C: Shaking creates loud noises that startle resting patients
options.D: Shaking causes the fabric to stretch out of shape quickly

explanation: Correct! Shaking soiled sheets sends germs and dust flying into the air, which can easily spread infection around the ward. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h2)

question: How can you tell if a correlation on a scatter diagram is strong?

options.A: The data points cluster tightly together along a clear path

options.C: The line on the graph goes straight up and down
options.D: There are more than one hundred dots on the chart

question: What is the main difference between a target population and an accessible population?

options.D: The target population is the ideal group, while the accessible group can actually be reached

question: Which type of infection control precautions must you practice with every single patient you care for?

options.A: Airborne precautions

options.D: Standard precautions

question: Which factor is most important when deciding if a psychiatric patient is ready for parole?

options.A: Having a high-paying job lined up before leaving

options.C: Completing a college degree during the hospital stay
options.D: Stable symptoms and willingness to take medications

question: A patient has belly pain that normal scans cannot explain. What procedure is a doctor likely to suggest next?

options.A: Electrocardiogram

options.C: Barium swallow test
options.D: Diagnostic laparoscopy

explanation: Well done! When regular scans don't show the problem, a diagnostic laparoscopy lets the doctor look directly inside the abdomen to find out what is causing the pain. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h2)

question: What do we call an actual bruise of the brain tissue that comes with bleeding?

options.A: Contusion
options.B: Hematoma
options.C: Concussion
options.D: Transection

explanation: Spot on! A brain contusion is essentially a bruise on the brain itself. A concussion is different because it usually doesn't show physical tearing or structural damage on scans. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T13#GNS222_U3_T13_h3)

question: What makes a female Guinea worm burst open and release her babies into water?

options.A: Exposure to sunlight
options.B: Ingestion of antibiotics
options.C: High fever in the host
options.D: Contact with cold water

question: What happens in a 'concealed' type of placental abruption?

options.A: The separation occurs entirely at the edge of the placental disk

options.C: Blood flows rapidly through the cervix as bright red fluid
options.D: The placenta detaches silently without any pain or bleeding whatsoever

explanation: In a concealed abruption, blood gets trapped inside the uterus. This means external bleeding looks deceptively small while internal shock can develop quickly. Great job keeping this in mind! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h4)

question: What is the main job of sensory receptors in your nervous system?

options.A: To send final motor commands to skeletal muscles
options.B: To produce hormones that regulate body temperature
options.C: To monitor changes inside and outside the body
options.D: To integrate information inside the spinal cord

explanation: You've got this! Sensory receptors are like your body's watchmen—they catch what's happening around and inside you and report it back to the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h1)

question: Through which route do gases or vapors enter the bloodstream the fastest?

options.A: Inhalation
options.B: Subcutaneous contact
options.C: Ingestion
options.D: Skin absorption

explanation: You got it! Breathing in a gas sends it straight through the huge surface area of the lungs directly into the blood. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h3)

question: You notice a ventilated patient has no breath sounds on the left side and uneven chest movement. What should you suspect first?

options.B: The ventilator circuit tubing has a small external leak
options.C: The patient is experiencing a sudden drop in blood sugar
options.D: The breathing tube has slipped into the right main bronchus

question: Which of the following is NOT a common physical complication of severe, prolonged vomiting in pregnancy?

options.A: Electrolyte and acid-base imbalance
options.B: Esophageal tears from forceful retching
options.C: Acute kidney injury from dehydration
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Gestational diabetes is related to insulin resistance and glucose metabolism, not directly caused by vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h6)

question: Which stage of insect development is completely skipped when an insect goes through incomplete metamorphosis?

options.A: The egg stage
options.B: The adult stage
options.C: The pupal stage
options.D: The larval stage

explanation: Incomplete metamorphosis skips the resting pupa stage, moving straight from egg to nymph to adult. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h1)

question: A community nurse is caring for a client who uses herbal remedies alongside prescribed medication. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Ask open questions to understand the client's beliefs without judging

options.C: Tell the client immediately to throw away all their herbal remedies
options.D: Refuse to provide further care until the client stops home treatments

question: Why is careful pin-site care so important for a patient with an external fixator?

options.A: To encourage faster bone mineralization around the pin insertion sites

options.C: To stop the external metal frame from rusting over time
options.D: To prevent the skin from sticking permanently to the metal frame

question: Which drug route is usually used when you cannot find an emergency IV line?

options.A: Intraosseous (IO)
options.B: Oral tablet swallowed
options.C: Topical skin patch
options.D: Subcutaneous injection

explanation: When an IV is impossible, we can drill right into the bone marrow (IO) to deliver emergency drugs super fast into circulation. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h6)

question: What are the main germs responsible for common skin infections like boils and impetigo?

options.A: Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacilli
options.B: Staphylococcus and Streptococcus bacteria
options.C: Enteric viruses and parasites
options.D: Dermatophyte fungi and molds

explanation: Staph and Strep are the usual suspects behind those painful, pus-filled skin sores you see so often in clinic rotations. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h3)

question: A patient is asked to stand up from a chair, walk ten feet, turn around, and sit back down. What is this clinical observation called?

options.A: Pulmonary function trial
options.B: Cardiorespiratory stress exam
options.C: Get-Up-and-Go test
options.D: Neurological reflex screen

explanation: The Get-Up-and-Go test is a quick, practical way to evaluate a patient's balance, sit-to-stand transition, and walking stability. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h3)

question: What liquid solution is standard for preserving a skin biopsy sample on its way to the lab?

options.A: 10% neutral buffered formalin
options.B: Normal sterile saline solution
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide antiseptic
options.D: Isopropyl alcohol 70 percent

explanation: Neutral buffered formalin is the go-to liquid fixative. It stops the tissue from breaking down so the pathologist can examine the cells clearly. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T3#GNS213_U5_T3_h8)

question: When is the best time to initiate breastfeeding after an uncomplicated delivery?

options.A: Within the first hour of birth
options.B: Once the milk transitions to white
options.C: After twenty-four hours of rest
options.D: After the baby receives initial vaccines

explanation: Starting breastfeeding within the first hour takes advantage of the baby's alert state and helps milk production start smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h5)

question: What is the main reason hospitals try to build a 'blame-free' reporting culture?

options.A: To encourage staff to report errors and near misses honestly
options.B: To make sure negligent workers never face legal consequences
options.C: To hide hospital mistakes from government regulators
options.D: To reduce the amount of paperwork nurses must complete daily

explanation: When staff aren't terrified of punishment, they speak up about close calls and mistakes. That honesty is how we fix things and protect future patients! [learn more](GST319_U5_T2#GST319_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why is a secondary immune response so much faster than the first one?

options.A: White blood cells travel faster through the bloodstream in adults
options.B: Memory cells formed during the first exposure quickly recognize the invader
options.C: The pathogen becomes weaker every time it enters the human body
options.D: The liver produces extra blood proteins during a secondary infection

explanation: Memory B-cells never forget a face! When they see a familiar germ again, they multiply instantly and pump out antibodies without needing a slow learning phase. [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h5)

question: How do long-term high food prices contribute to chronic illnesses like diabetes and obesity in vulnerable communities?

options.A: By eliminating the body's natural ability to process natural sugars
options.B: By forcing families to rely heavily on cheap, highly processed, carbohydrate-heavy foods
options.C: By providing extra financial funds for families to buy excessive amounts of meat
options.D: By encouraging children to exercise less due to high grocery store bills

question: What is the main focus of end-of-life care when a patient is being cared for at home?

options.A: Complete reversal of chronic terminal diseases
options.B: Strict physical rehabilitation exercises
options.C: Aggressive curative surgeries and treatments
options.D: Comfort, pain control, and symptom management

explanation: Great job! At the end of life, the priority shifts completely from chasing cures to making sure the patient is free of pain and as comfortable as possible. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T1#GNS324_U3_T1_h8)

question: What is the biggest benefit of encouraging community participation in health programs?

options.A: It removes the need for trained professional nurses and doctors entirely
options.B: It allows the government to avoid spending any money on healthcare infrastructure
options.C: It shifts all legal liability for illness outbreaks onto local villagers
options.D: It builds local ownership and ensures long-term sustainability of the programs

explanation: When a community feels 'this project is ours,' they will take care of it and keep it running long after outside help leaves. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is a rate more useful than a simple count when comparing disease frequency between a large city and a small village?

options.A: A rate only counts people who are admitted to private hospitals
options.B: A rate adjusts for differences in total population size
options.C: A simple count is always illegal to use in public health
options.D: A rate completely eliminates the need for data collection

question: What type of vaginal discharge would a nurse expect to see in a patient with acute postpartum endometritis?

options.A: Dry with no fluid present
options.B: Foul-smelling and purulent
options.C: Clear, watery, and odorless
options.D: Thick, white, and cottage-cheese-like

question: What is the primary role of the nurse when patients want to use complementary or alternative therapies?

options.B: Personally performing massage and aromatherapy for every single patient
options.C: Ensuring safe use, providing education, and supporting patient preferences
options.D: Selling herbal supplements to patients to help fund the hospital ward

explanation: Well done! Nurses act as educators and safety advocates, helping patients safely blend alternative methods with their standard medical care. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is usually the very first step when preparing to study a community?

options.D: Purchasing expensive medical equipment for the local clinic

question: What is the primary purpose of giving antiretroviral prophylaxis to a newborn exposed to HIV?

options.A: To prevent infection from any virus acquired during delivery

options.C: To cure any congenital birth defects present at birth
options.D: To boost the infant's natural vitamin absorption levels

explanation: Infant prophylaxis acts as a protective shield, clearing any viral particles that may have entered the baby's system during childbirth. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h6)

question: What is the term for physical pregnancy symptoms, like nausea, that are sometimes experienced by expectant fathers?

options.A: Couvade syndrome

options.C: Quickening response
options.D: Maternal ambivalence

question: Which of these is NOT a good public health strategy for preventing birth defects?

options.A: Encouraging the use of unregulated herbal mixtures during pregnancy
options.B: Promoting rubella vaccinations
options.C: Ensuring women attend regular antenatal care
options.D: Educating communities about the risks of close-relative marriages

question: Which of these is a classic example of a negative feedback loop?

options.A: Regulating body temperature through sweating
options.B: Releasing oxytocin during childbirth contractions
options.C: Rapidly nursing an infant to increase milk flow
options.D: Forming a hard blood clot over a skin wound

explanation: Sweating is a classic negative feedback response. When you get too hot, your body works to cool you down, bringing things back to normal! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is keeping a close eye on fluids and electrolytes a top nursing priority for enteric fever patients?

options.C: Patients are forbidden from drinking water
options.D: Antibiotics automatically cause total kidney failure

question: A working mother needs daytime care for her two-year-old toddler. Which facility type is most appropriate?

options.A: An adult day care centre

options.C: A residential boarding home
options.D: An infant and toddler nursery

question: A patient stumbles when walking and cannot coordinate their finger-to-nose movement during a physical exam. Which brain structure is most likely impaired?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Thalamus
options.C: Cerebellum

question: Why is Guinea worm disease such a big problem for farming villages?

options.C: It destroys livestock and crops stored in the village
options.D: It inflicts crippling pain that stops people from farming

question: Which of the following is an example of an internalizing intentional injury?

options.A: Physical assault

question: What is the basic functional unit of the kidney called?

options.A: Neuron
options.B: Lobule
options.C: Alveolus
options.D: Nephron

question: How does continuous on-the-job training help primary healthcare workers?

question: If an epi curve shows multiple waves spaced out by the exact incubation period of an illness, what kind of outbreak is it?

question: Within how many hours must Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) be started to reduce HIV risk after an exposure?

options.A: Within 24 hours

options.C: Within 72 hours
options.D: Within 7 days

question: Why might a surgeon need to perform a craniectomy (removing a piece of the skull) after severe brain trauma?

question: Why can the Widal test sometimes give misleading results in places where typhoid is common?

question: Why is it important to store dry goods in clean, pest-proof containers off the floor?

question: Why is writing accurate and prompt notes so crucial in an intensive care setting?

options.A: It allows family members to edit the medical chart from home

options.C: It guarantees that the hospital insurance claim will never be denied
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal handoffs during shift changes entirely

explanation: ICU patients change fast! Good documentation ensures that the next nurse or doctor stepping into the unit knows exactly what happened and how the patient responded. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T8#GNS321_U2_T8_h7)

question: What must a nurse do when they suspect an older adult is being abused at home?

options.C: Wait until absolute proof is gathered before telling anyone else
options.D: Advise the patient to handle the situation independently

question: What is the name of the muscular food pipe that connects your throat to your stomach?

question: Which body changes in older adults greatly affect how drugs leave the body?

question: Why do we reference sources in nursing writing?

question: Which of these is a classic sign of mastitis in a breastfeeding mother?

question: What is the main chart midwives use during labor to track progress and catch problems early?

options.D: Otoscope

explanation: Correct! The partograph is a simple yet powerful graphical chart that helps us monitor labor and spot when things are taking too long. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h4)

question: Why are direct-acting vasodilators often given along with a beta-blocker?

question: What does the acronym PMTCT stand for in healthcare?

options.D: Pediatric Management of Therapeutic Care and Treatment

question: Which insect transmits the parasite that causes onchocerciasis to humans?

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a gastric lavage on a patient?

question: A nurse is checking a patient's foot sensation for diabetes care. What is the right way to test light touch?

options.C: Use a warm metal tuning fork to check for vibration sense only.
options.D: Press firmly with the thumb until the patient reports aching pain.

explanation: Spot on! Using a monofilament while the patient closes their eyes stops them from guessing and tests those light surface receptors accurately. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T5#GNS211_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is your main nursing worry when a patient is given insulin for diabetes?

options.A: Monitoring for a sudden dangerous drop in blood sugar
options.B: Ensuring the patient's blood pressure does not rise too high
options.C: Assessing the patient for sudden changes in heart rhythm
options.D: Checking the patient for signs of a severe bacterial infection

explanation: Insulin sweeps glucose out of the blood and into cells. If food intake doesn't match, blood sugar can drop dangerously low (hypoglycemia). [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h6)

question: As a nurse explaining a treatment plan, what should you avoid doing?

options.A: Using heavy medical jargon that the patient does not understand
options.B: Ensuring the conversation remains strictly confidential
options.C: Explaining the importance of abstaining from sex during treatment
options.D: Asking the patient about her current sexual partners

explanation: Always keep it simple! Heavy medical grammar just confuses patients. Talk to them in clear, everyday language they can easily grasp. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the golden rule when a nurse has to break tragic news of a death to family members?

options.A: Use clear, direct, and compassionate language
options.B: Ask another family member to break the news
options.C: Use complex medical terms to soften the blow
options.D: Delay the information until they stop crying

explanation: That's right! Being clear and direct avoids any confusion, ensuring the family understands the reality while feeling your compassion. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h4)

question: What condition involves widespread, abnormal blood clotting followed by severe bleeding due to used-up clotting factors?

options.A: Chronic venous insufficiency
options.B: Pulmonary hypertension
options.C: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
options.D: Acute respiratory distress syndrome

explanation: DIC is a serious complication where small clots form throughout the body, eventually exhausting clotting proteins and causing severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why is collaboration between schools and local primary health centers important?

options.A: It creates a smooth referral pathway for immunization and clinical care
options.B: It allows the school to take over full control of the clinic
options.C: It stops community members from seeking traditional medicine
options.D: It ensures that students never have to visit a hospital again

explanation: Local health centers provide backup support for vaccination drives, medical referrals, and complex treatments beyond school capacity. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which health issue puts an HIV-positive patient into WHO Clinical Stage 4?

options.A: A normal CD4 count with no physical complaints
options.B: Kaposi sarcoma or severe opportunistic infections
options.C: Recurrent common colds and mild skin rashes
options.D: Persistent generalized swollen lymph nodes only

explanation: Spot on! Stage 4 involves severe illnesses and indicator conditions that mark advanced HIV disease (AIDS). [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h5)

question: A pregnant patient at 28 weeks is tired, and tests show true iron deficiency. Where did most of her missing iron go?

options.A: Stored permanently inside the maternal liver cells
options.B: To the developing fetus and the placenta
options.C: Excreted rapidly through the gastrointestinal tract
options.D: Lost entirely through excessive maternal sweating

explanation: The growing baby always gets first priority! The baby and placenta draw a lot of iron from the mother to build their own systems. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h2)

question: Which of these everyday nursing actions is an example of medical asepsis?

options.A: Performing an open surgical operation in the theatre
options.B: Wiping down a bedside table with a disinfectant wipe
options.C: Putting on sterile surgical gloves and a gown
options.D: Inserting a urinary catheter using a sterile kit

explanation: Great job! Medical asepsis is all about clean habits—like wiping down surfaces to cut down on germs. Surgical asepsis is what we save for deep, sterile procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is a major goal of community blood pressure screening programs?

options.A: To distribute free surgical equipment to local residents
options.B: To diagnose and treat rare genetic skin disorders
options.C: To replace hospital emergency rooms entirely
options.D: To identify undiagnosed hypertension early before complications occur

explanation: You got it! Since hypertension is 'silent,' community screenings help catch it early so we can prevent strokes and heart attacks. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T2#GNS313_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why does dead heart muscle (necrosis) increase the risk of the heart wall tearing open?

options.A: Dead tissue instantly turns into hard bone
options.B: Dead muscle tissue loses its strength and tears easily under pressure
options.C: Dead cells make the heart grow too fast
options.D: Blood pressure inside the heart drops to zero

explanation: When heart muscle dies during a heart attack, it turns into a soft, weak spot. Just like a worn-out bicycle tire, that weak spot can blow out under normal pumping pressure. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T14#GNS213_U1_T14_h6)

question: Your patient has dry skin, blurry vision, can't pass urine, and seems quite confused after taking an unknown drug. What toxidrome are they showing?

options.A: Anticholinergic
options.B: Sedative-hypnotic
options.C: Sympathomimetic
options.D: Cholinergic

explanation: Think of anticholinergic drugs as drying up all the body's moisture—hence the dry skin, urinary retention, and blurry vision, plus a confused mind! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T6#GNS215_U5_T6_h2)

question: Which group of blood pressure medications must be strictly avoided during pregnancy because they can harm the baby's kidneys?

options.A: Beta-blockers
options.B: Calcium channel blockers
options.C: ACE inhibitors
options.D: Centrally acting alpha agonists

explanation: Remember: ACE inhibitors are known to mess with how a baby's kidneys develop, so doctors steer clear of them during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T007#GNS226_U4_T007_h5)

question: Which maternal blood vessels are opened up by the placenta to bathe the fetal villi in nutrient-rich blood?

options.A: Cardinal veins
options.B: Uterine veins
options.C: Umbilical arteries
options.D: Spiral arteries

explanation: Spot on! The trophoblast gently remodels the mother's spiral arteries so that blood pools nicely around the baby's villi for easy sharing. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T4#GNS121_U6_T4_h4)

question: What does a flattening weight curve on a child's growth chart usually mean first?

options.A: Normal physical growth for that specific age
options.B: An early warning sign of a developing problem
options.C: A measurement error by the attending nurse
options.D: A sudden increase in daily physical activity

explanation: Spot on! When the weight line flattens out, it's often the very first clue that nutrition or health is slipping, even before the child looks visibly thin. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T54#GNS214_U1_T54_h3)

question: A ward manager notices missed medication doses and sloppy handovers. What is the most likely underlying issue?

options.A: Low staff morale and diminished workplace motivation
options.B: An unexpected surplus of advanced diagnostic medical equipment
options.C: Excessively high patient satisfaction survey scores
options.D: Too many mandatory training workshops on patient empathy

explanation: When morale dips low, even simple daily routines like handovers can start slipping. Recognizing this helps us support one another better. [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is a major role of state-level primary health care bodies in Nigeria?

options.A: Building private international airports
options.B: Collecting local market taxes for traditional rulers
options.C: Appointing village chiefs in rural communities
options.D: Supervising LGA activities and procuring bulk medical supplies

explanation: State bodies provide mid-level oversight, supporting local governments with supplies, training, and technical guidance. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h5)

question: What happens to spermatids during the spermiogenesis phase?

options.A: They remodel their shape and develop a tail without dividing again
options.B: They combine with fluid from the prostate gland
options.C: They multiply rapidly through standard cell division
options.D: They travel out of the scrotum into the urinary bladder

explanation: Spermiogenesis is purely a structural remodeling phase where round cells transform into streamlined swimming sperm. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h4)

question: What does the top number in a blood pressure reading represent?

options.A: Systolic pressure when the heart rests
options.B: Systolic pressure when the heart beats
options.C: Diastolic pressure when the heart rests
options.D: Diastolic pressure when the heart beats

explanation: The top number is the systolic pressure, which measures the force in the arteries when the heart contracts or beats. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h1)

question: How does the daily objective of a public health nurse differ from that of a bedside hospital nurse?

options.A: The public health nurse focuses on disease prevention for populations, while the bedside nurse focuses on acute care for individuals
options.B: The public health nurse diagnoses surgical conditions, while the bedside nurse only administers oral medications
options.C: The public health nurse works exclusively with doctors, while the bedside nurse works completely alone
options.D: The public health nurse ignores chronic illnesses, while the bedside nurse only handles emergency trauma

explanation: The core distinction lies in the population-wide prevention mindset of public health versus the individual-focused healing mindset of clinical care. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which chart is best for showing how patient vital signs change over time?

options.A: Frequency table
options.B: Pie chart
options.C: Bar chart
options.D: Line graph

explanation: You got it! Whenever you want to track changes over a timeline—like hourly blood pressure readings—a line graph is your best friend. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T2#GNS217_U4_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical safety hazard inside an operating room?

options.A: Sharps injuries from needles and scalpel blades
options.B: Electrical risks from high-powered surgical equipment
options.C: Chemical exposure from waste anesthetic gases
options.D: High-speed public traffic noise from outside the hospital

explanation: You got it! Operating rooms are quiet and sound-proofed. The real worries inside are things like sharps, chemicals, and electrical hazards. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the proper name for the normal vaginal discharge that follows childbirth?

options.A: Mecronium
options.B: Pruritus
options.C: Colostrum
options.D: Lochia

explanation: Spot on! Lochia is just the normal cleansing flow from the uterus made of blood, mucus, and tissue that changes appearance over the first few weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T021#GNS226_U3_T021_h2)

question: Who are the key community gatekeepers a nurse should involve to help change harmful food taboos?

options.A: Foreign tourists visiting the local village market
options.B: Commercial transport drivers operating local buses
options.C: Traditional rulers, religious leaders, and elder matriarchs
options.D: Construction workers building new community roads

explanation: Working with respected community figures bridges the gap smoothly between modern health education and traditional beliefs. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h7)

question: A patient complains of chest pain and trouble swallowing because their food pipe is squeezing in an uncoordinated way. What is this called?

options.A: Oesophageal varices
options.B: Hiatus hernia
options.C: Oesophageal spasm
options.D: Mallory-Weiss tear

question: According to the Spaulding classification, what level of processing is required for surgical instruments?

options.A: Basic washing with soap
options.B: High-level disinfection
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: Low-level disinfection

explanation: Surgical instruments are classified as critical items because they enter sterile tissues, so they must be fully sterilized. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: What triggers the sarcoplasmic reticulum to release a flood of calcium inside a heart cell?

options.A: A small influx of extracellular calcium through membrane channels
options.B: The direct binding of ATP molecules to troponin C
options.C: The sudden drop in intracellular potassium levels
options.D: A massive flood of sodium ions directly from the T-tubules

explanation: It is a chain reaction! A little calcium trickles in from the outside, which triggers a much bigger release of stored calcium inside. Neat, right? [learn more](GNS121_U3_T10#GNS121_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing disposable syringes
options.B: To speed up medication administration during busy ward shifts
options.C: To ensure patients experience zero pain during every procedure
options.D: To prevent harm to patients, healthcare workers, and the community

explanation: Injection safety encompasses protective measures for everyone involved in or affected by the injection process, preventing infections and injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is a direct result of poor nutrition in an older adult going through rehabilitation?

options.A: Delayed wound healing and increased muscle weakness
options.B: Enhanced immune system function
options.C: Instant recovery from chronic stroke symptoms
options.D: Rapid muscle growth and increased strength

question: A patient with a broken leg complains of throbbing pain and winces when moving. Which option is a great nursing diagnosis focus?

options.A: Fracture of the right tibia and fibula bones
options.B: Prescription of narcotic pain medication
options.C: Surgical repair of the lower leg bones
options.D: Acute pain related to physical tissue trauma

question: A patient with long-term diabetes complains of blurry vision and dark spots. Which eye problem should you suspect first?

options.A: Acute glaucoma
options.B: Retinal detachment
options.C: Nuclear cataracts
options.D: Diabetic retinopathy

explanation: Well done! Years of high blood sugar can damage the small blood vessels in the retina, making diabetic retinopathy a very common cause of vision changes. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T13#GNS324_U4_T13_h2)

question: A nurse is getting a patient ready for a speculum exam. What is the best way to help her prepare?

question: What is the main job of anti-spasmodic drugs in the tummy?

options.C: To speed up the transit time of stool in the colon
options.D: To relax overactive smooth muscle and relieve cramps

explanation: Think of anti-spasmodics as a calming massage for your gut muscles. They help stop those painful, tight cramps when the tummy muscles are working into overdrive! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why might a doctor draw fluid out of a painful joint (arthrocentesis)?

options.A: To inject fresh cartilage directly into the space
options.B: To remove all the bone spurs permanently
options.C: To rule out infection or gout by analyzing the fluid
options.D: To measure the exact thickness of the bone

question: Which symptom should a nurse teach a patient with dysmenorrhoea to report immediately?

options.A: Feeling tired and needing extra sleep during bleeding
options.B: Mild lower abdominal cramping on the first day of menses
options.C: Sudden high fever and foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.D: A slight decrease in appetite during the menstrual cycle

explanation: You got it! Fever and foul discharge are red flags for an infection, which means it's not just regular period pain and needs urgent attention. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h8)

question: Which of these is an important warning sign you must teach a patient before they go home after a proctoscopy?

options.A: Normal resumption of eating food
options.B: Heavy or continuous rectal bleeding
options.C: Mild passing of gas for two hours
options.D: A temporary feeling of rectal fullness

question: What is the big advantage of using a moist cold compress instead of a stiff ice pack?

options.A: They require no refrigeration or ice whatsoever
options.B: They completely eliminate the risk of frostbite
options.C: They mold easily to uneven body contours like the jaw or face
options.D: They stay warm for up to twelve hours at a time

explanation: You got it! Faces and jaws aren't flat, so a flexible moist compress hugs those tricky curves much better than a rigid ice pack. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T8#GNS221_U3_T8_h4)

question: A rural clinic nurse finds that many women prefer giving birth at home. What is the best first step for the nurse?

options.A: Engage community leaders and educate women on the safety of facility delivery
options.B: Report all pregnant women who plan home births to the local police
options.C: Close the clinic until the women agree to come in voluntarily
options.D: Ignore the practice since home delivery has no real risks

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with village leaders builds trust and helps women see the safety and benefits of delivering at a health facility. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h8)

question: What is the primary danger of untreated prolonged obstructed labor?

options.A: Postpartum hair loss

options.C: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.D: Gestational diabetes

question: A patient comes to the clinic struggling with a weak urine stream after a past pelvic injury. What procedure are they most likely getting ready for?

options.A: Gastric tube insertion
options.B: Urethral dilation
options.C: Endotracheal intubation
options.D: Esophageal manometry

question: Which two main blood vessel systems supply oxygenated blood to the brain?

options.A: Brachiocephalic and thoracic trunks
options.B: Coronary and pulmonary arteries
options.C: Internal carotid and vertebral arteries
options.D: Subclavian and jugular vessels

question: Which level of prevention uses routine immunizations to stop a disease before it even starts?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention

options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Spot on! Primary prevention is all about stopping health problems before they begin—vaccines are a classic example. Brilliant work! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h5)

question: A patient's prostate-specific antigen (PSA) blood test comes back a little high. What should you as a nurse keep in mind?

options.A: It is a definitive confirmation that malignant prostate cancer is present
options.B: It proves the patient has a severe urinary tract infection
options.C: It can be elevated due to benign growth, infection, or recent manipulation
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will require immediate surgical removal

explanation: Remember, PSA is sensitive to lots of things! A simple infection, a routine exam, or just natural aging (BPH) can make PSA go up, not just cancer. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the main goal of having a multi-sectoral referral network for GBV survivors?

options.A: To provide comprehensive medical, legal, and social support through coordinated agencies
options.B: To reduce the total number of follow-up medical visits required
options.C: To transfer all administrative responsibilities away from the hospital
options.D: To ensure the police handle every aspect of the patient's recovery

explanation: Healing takes a village! Teamwork between health workers, legal aid, and social services gives survivors the best all-round support. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h7)

question: Why is just treating medical symptoms often not enough for a community?

options.A: Patients refuse to visit primary health care clinics unless accompanied by local leaders
options.B: Environmental and social root causes like poor water or housing will keep causing new illnesses
options.C: Doctors usually prescribe the wrong medications for community outbreaks
options.D: Medical treatments are too expensive for the government to maintain long-term

explanation: Spot on! If we treat a patient in the clinic but send them back to drink contaminated water, they'll just fall sick again. We have to fix the environment too! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h1)

question: What is the medical definition of a fracture?

options.A: A stretching injury to the ligaments surrounding a joint
options.B: A complete break or crack in the continuity of a bone
options.C: An infection located deep inside the bone marrow
options.D: A sudden tear in the muscle fibers attached to bone

question: What makes SIMV (Synchronized Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation) different from Assist-Control mode?

options.C: It completely stops the patient from taking independent breaths
options.D: It allows the patient to breathe spontaneously between mandatory machine breaths

question: What is the main goal of Human Resource Management (HRM) in a hospital?

options.A: Determining the hospital financial budget for the year
options.B: Repairing and maintaining hospital medical equipment
options.C: Managing staff from recruitment to retirement
options.D: Purchasing drugs and medical supplies for the pharmacy

explanation: Think of HR as the backbone for the people side of healthcare! HRM takes care of staff members right from when they apply for a job all the way to when they retire. [learn more](GST321_U4_T1#GST321_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which syndrome is famously linked with missing female reproductive structures like the uterus or tubes?

options.A: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome

question: Why is a needs assessment the first step in planning a community nutrition program?

options.A: To find out what specific nutritional problems the community actually faces
options.B: To punish local markets for selling poor quality food
options.C: To decide which nurses will be fired if goals fail
options.D: To secure funding from international banks immediately

question: Why is counting journal download numbers alone not enough to prove a study was clinically successful?

options.C: It means the hospital administration will refuse to read the document

question: What is the primary function of planning in nursing management?

options.A: It is used strictly to discipline underperforming ward staff.

question: What are the classic early symptoms of an unruptured ectopic pregnancy?

question: Which condition makes the rectal route unsafe because of a high risk of bleeding?

options.B: Simple upper respiratory infection

options.D: Chronic ankle swelling

question: What is a major social barrier that prevents Nigerian teenagers from seeking care?

options.A: Fear of community gossip and moral judgment from adults
options.B: Excessive availability of youth-only private hospitals everywhere
options.C: Mandatory free transport provided by local government councils
options.D: Strict laws requiring teenagers to study nursing in secondary school

question: How do medicines like tranexamic acid help control bleeding?

question: A community health nurse wants to understand why mothers refuse to bring babies for routine immunization. Which data collection method is best suited for this?

options.A: Measuring the height and weight of newborn babies
options.B: Checking the expiration dates of vaccines in the clinic fridge
options.C: Counting the number of cars passing through the main highway

question: What important advice should you give a patient with hyperparathyroidism who is waiting for surgery?

question: What is the very first step when solving a problem?

options.D: Blaming the staff member who made the error

question: What major global health target was famously set by the Alma-Ata Declaration?

question: Why are home-based antenatal visits especially helpful for women living in rural areas?

question: Why is seeing a patient at home more revealing than seeing them in a hospital clinic?

question: Why is it risky to assume sudden confusion in an older adult is just 'normal aging'?

question: What type of stimuli does our sense of smell (olfaction) pick up?

question: Why do many patients managing chronic NCDs also need psychological support?

question: Why does the human brain have many folds, or gyri and sulci?

question: Why must the tools used to cut the umbilical cord be strictly sterile?

question: A hospital pharmacy prices an antibiotic by adding up the supplier price, shipping fees, storage power, and dispensing salaries. What costing approach is this?

question: What is the most important safety action before turning a patient to one side during an occupied bed change?

question: Which lung issue is most common for a patient stuck on prolonged bed rest in traction?

question: What is usually one of the very first warning signs a woman might notice with cervical cancer?

question: For couples under 35 years old, how long of regular, unprotected sex without pregnancy is usually needed before diagnosing infertility?

question: What is a key difference between the anterior and posterior pituitary lobes?

question: A patient with a family history of brain degeneration starts accusing relatives of stealing items they just misplaced. What is this called?

question: What makes a disease communicable?

question: What happens to a patient's metabolic rate during severe physiological stress like major trauma or sepsis?

question: Your patient just returned to the ward after a modified radical mastectomy. What is a key nursing action to prevent lymphedema?

question: Why is educating community and religious leaders an effective way to fight child trafficking?

question: You check a toddler's growth chart and notice their weight curve has suddenly crossed downward across two major percentile lines. What should you suspect?

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of using a partograph during labor?

question: Why is checking a patient's pulse such a useful assessment tool in daily nursing care?

question: What is an effective communication technique when talking to a client with a neurologic speech delay?

question: Why is it smart to check back on a patient shortly after giving them a new intravenous drug?

question: Why is it crucial for nurses to monitor a patient's urine output in the hours following an IVP?

question: Why might a patient with a degenerative nerve disease be given an antidepressant along with their other medications?

question: Which of these is NOT a physical danger faced by waste handlers in the hospital?

question: Which of the following is a common positive result of using person-centered care?

question: Why must nurses look beyond the individual adolescent patient during clinical assessments?

question: Which of these is a major barrier to using research in many Nigerian hospitals?

question: What is a common misconception about the 'controlling' function in nursing?

question: A patient comes in complaining of severe tiredness, unexpected weight gain, and feeling cold all the time. Which hormone issue is likely going on?

question: A patient with post-traumatic stress disorder startles violently at a sudden loud noise. Which limbic structure is most likely driving this hyperactive reaction?

options.D: Keeping essential medicines affordable

question: Which lab finding is a well-known kidney side effect of long-term D-penicillamine use?

options.A: Hyponatremia
options.B: Proteinuria
options.C: Hyperglycemia
options.D: Hyperbilirubinemia

explanation: Thiol drugs can sometimes irritate the delicate filtering units of the kidneys, causing protein to leak into the urine (proteinuria). Regular checks keep patients safe! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T4#GNS223_U8_T4_h5)

question: A nurse wants to assess how community members handle their household drinking water. Which method is most appropriate?

options.A: Calculating annual hospital mortality statistics
options.B: Analyzing international disease journals
options.C: Reading national population census booklets
options.D: Direct observation of water storage practices

explanation: Direct observation allows the nurse to see actual daily behaviors regarding water handling rather than relying on reported answers. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h3)

question: A young student in Nigeria worries that taking Postinor-2 will make her barren. How should you respond?

options.A: Prescribe a strong surgical procedure to clear her reproductive system
options.B: Scold her for engaging in premarital sex and refuse to give her the medication
options.C: Gently educate her with facts, explaining that the drug does not cause permanent infertility
options.D: Agree with her fears and advise her never to use any form of family planning

explanation: Market myths can be scary! Gently talking clients through the facts builds trust and ensures they get safe, accurate reproductive healthcare. You're going to be an amazing nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h8)

question: What causes platelets to stick together and form a temporary plug at an injury site?

options.A: A sudden drop in the overall body temperature
options.B: Contact with exposed collagen and released chemical messengers
options.C: An increase in red blood cell production by the liver
options.D: The direct action of white blood cells on the vessel wall

explanation: When platelets touch exposed collagen under the damaged endothelium, they activate, change shape, and release chemicals that attract more platelets to build the plug. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which of the following is a non-pharmacological method for managing physical discomfort?

options.A: Providing an intravenous pain medication
options.B: Increasing the dosage of muscle relaxants
options.C: Applying heat or cold therapy
options.D: Administering a strong narcotic pill

explanation: Heat and cold therapy are physical comfort measures that do not involve drugs and help soothe aching muscles and joints. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h7)

question: What makes an abortion 'unsafe' according to public health standards?

options.A: A termination done without proper surgical tools or skilled personnel
options.B: Any abortion performed after the first trimester of pregnancy
options.C: Any pregnancy loss that occurs naturally without human intervention
options.D: A medical termination using only prescription oral medications

explanation: Spot on! Unsafe abortions happen when procedures are done by untrained hands or in bad conditions, putting mothers at huge risk of injury. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h1)

question: A patient with ALS is having muscle weakness and wasting. Which part of the nervous system is mainly affected?

options.A: The myelin sheath of peripheral nerves
options.B: Upper and lower motor neurons
options.C: Dopamine receptors in the basal ganglia
options.D: Sensory nerve endings in the skin

explanation: ALS attacks the motor neurons that tell your muscles to move. When these cells weaken, the muscles waste away (atrophy). You are building fantastic clinical knowledge! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h3)

question: Why would a doctor order an antibody blood test for someone with a suspected endocrine problem?

options.A: To test how quickly the kidneys filter out waste products
options.B: To determine if the patient has a bacterial infection
options.C: To check for autoimmune destruction of endocrine tissue
options.D: To measure the exact weight and size of the pituitary gland

explanation: Spot on! Antibody tests help us see if the body's immune system is mistakenly attacking its own hormone glands, like in thyroid disorders. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h2)

question: What HbA1c blood test result is generally used to diagnose diabetes?

options.A: 8.0% or higher
options.B: 10.5% or higher
options.D: 6.5% or higher

explanation: An HbA1c of 6.5% or higher shows that blood sugar has been running high over the past three months. It's a key lab value you'll use all the time in practice! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is a direct benefit of using research-backed repositioning schedules on the ward?

options.A: An increase in daily patient discharge rates
options.B: A reduction in hospital-acquired pressure ulcers
options.C: Fewer mandatory shifts for junior nurses
options.D: Lower hospital electricity and utility bills

explanation: You got it! Studies on skin care clearly show that turning patients on a structured schedule keeps their skin safe and prevents painful bedsores. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h4)

question: A pregnant woman tests positive for HIV at her first ANC visit. What is the most important first step to protect her baby?

options.A: Advise her to avoid all forms of physical exercise
options.B: Schedule an immediate cesarean section delivery
options.C: Start her on antiretroviral therapy right away
options.D: Recommend immediate weaning after birth

explanation: You got it! Starting ART early drops her viral load, which is the absolute best way to keep the baby HIV-free. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T9#GNS216_U6_T9_h6)
